facts.raw_span: 6-month history of progressive neck pain radiating to his left hand
pain was described as electrical in nature
numbness in the C8–T1 dermatomes
weakness in fine movements and a weak grip of the left hand
marked atrophy of the hypothenar and interosseous muscles of the left hand
muscle strength of 3/5
marked osteolysis and collapse of the T1 vertebra
extensive paravertebral soft tissue component
lesion was intermediate to low signal on T1-weighted images
lesion was intermediate on T2-weighted images
lesion showed heterogeneous enhancement after gadolinium administration
lesion involved the anterior and posterior longitudinal ligaments

concepts.why: The patient's presentation of progressive neck pain, numbness in the C8-T1 dermatomes, and weakness in fine movements, combined with imaging findings of marked osteolysis and collapse of the T1 vertebra, are consistent with a chordoma.
The patient's imaging findings of marked osteolysis and collapse of the T1 vertebra, with an extensive paravertebral soft tissue component, are consistent with an osteosarcoma.

The patient's presentation of progressive neck pain, numbness in the C8-T1 dermatomes, and weakness in fine movements, combined with imaging findings of marked osteolysis and collapse of the T1 vertebra, are consistent with a spinal metastasis.
The patient's imaging findings of marked osteolysis and collapse of the T1 vertebra, with an extensive paravertebral soft tissue component, are consistent with discitis.

The patient's presentation of progressive neck pain, numbness in the C8-T1 dermatomes, and weakness in fine movements, combined with imaging findings of marked osteolysis and collapse of the T1 vertebra, are consistent with spondylodiscitis.

The patient's presentation of weakness in fine movements and a weak grip of the left hand, combined with imaging findings of marked atrophy of the hypothenar and interosseous muscles, are consistent with rheumatoid arthritis.

The patient's presentation of weakness in fine movements and a weak grip of the left hand, combined with imaging findings of marked atrophy of the hypothenar and interosseous muscles, are consistent with ankylosing spondylitis.
The patient's presentation of numbness in the C8-T1 dermatomes, weakness in fine movements, and a weak grip of the left hand, are consistent with spinal stenosis.

rationales.F05: Muscle atrophy is more typical of primary bone tumors like chordoma or osteosarcoma.
rationales.F06: Muscle weakness is more typical of primary bone tumors like chordoma or osteosarcoma.
rationales.F07: Osteolysis and vertebral collapse are more typical of aggressive primary bone tumors like chordoma or osteosarcoma, or spinal metastasis.
rationales.F12: Involvement of the anterior and posterior longitudinal ligaments is more typical of primary bone tumors like chordoma or osteosarcoma.
